method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Use non-pharmacological methods (play therapy, distraction) as alternatives or adjuncts, and topical, local or regional anaesthesia where appropriate** (eg Bier block).
claims.source_text: Use non-pharmacological methods, such as play therapy and distraction techniques, as alternatives or adjuncts … Topical agents, local or regional anaesthesia should be used if appropriate (eg Bier block)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ensure adequate analgesia and watch for the combined effect of sedation and opioid.**
claims.source_text: Ensure adequate analgesia and monitor for combined effects of sedation and opiate analgesia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Only clinicians trained and approved in paediatric sedation**, experienced in paediatric resuscitation, airway management and monitoring, should use sedation agents.
claims.source_text: Sedation agents should only be used by clinicians who are trained and approved in their use in children and who have experience in paediatric resuscitation, airway management and monitoring
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sedatives can cause airway compromise, respiratory depression and CNS depression**, so careful monitoring and skilled staff are essential.
claims.source_text: Medications used in procedural sedation may cause a wide range of side-effects, including airway compromise and respiratory depression, as well as depression of the central nervous system, requiring careful monitoring and skilled response … Appropriately trained staff skilled in airway management are essential
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-sedation:** review need and urgency, risk factors and contraindications · consent from the child (if appropriate) and parents · **fasting per local guidelines** · analgesia for painful procedures · **sedation checklist with role assignment** · prepare equipment · **agree a plan B for sedation failure.**
claims.source_text: Review the need for procedural sedation and its urgency Review patient risk factors and contraindications relevant to that child and the drug being used (see below) Obtain consent from the child (if appropriate) and their parent(s)/carer(s) Fasting times (see local fasting guidelines) … Provide analgesia for potentially painful procedures Use a sedation checklist and role assignment … Prepare equipment and environment Discuss a 'plan B' in the event of sedation failure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Resuscitation equipment and staff competent in paediatric resuscitation and airway management must be readily available before starting.**
claims.source_text: Resuscitation equipment and staff competent in paediatric resuscitation and airway management and monitoring must be readily available prior to commencing procedural sedation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not proceed** if child, clinician or environment factors make sedation or the procedure unsafe.
claims.source_text: Unsafe to proceed with sedation and/or procedure due to any of the following: Child factors … Clinician factors … Environment/location factors
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Higher risk of severe adverse effects: seek senior clinician or specialist advice on risk versus benefit.**
claims.source_text: The following conditions are associated with increased risk of severe adverse effects of procedural sedation. Consultation with senior clinician/specialist advice is essential to discuss the risk versus benefit of performing procedural sedation in these children:
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Airway:** severe obstructive airway disease (croup, foreign body, head and facial trauma); previous airway surgery, laryngomalacia, craniofacial abnormality. **Breathing:** severe respiratory distress (pneumonia, bronchiolitis, asthma); sleep apnoea.
claims.source_text: Airway Acute: severe obstructive airway disease, eg croup, foreign body, head and facial trauma Past history: previous airway surgery, laryngomalacia, craniofacial abnormalities Breathing Acute: severe respiratory distress, eg pneumonia, bronchiolitis, exacerbation of asthma Past History: sleep apnoea
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Circulation:** shock; congenital heart disease. **Neurological:** altered consciousness, seizure, meningitis, trauma, space-occupying lesion; unstable epilepsy, neuromuscular disease. **Other:** unstable psychiatric disorder; previous sedation failure or anaesthetic reaction.
claims.source_text: Circulation Acute: circulatory compromise, eg shock Past history: congenital cardiac disease Neurological Acute: altered level of consciousness, seizure, meningitis, trauma, space occupying lesion Past history: unstable epilepsy, neuromuscular disease Other Acute: unstable psychiatric disorder Past history: previous sedation failure or anaesthetic reaction
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choice depends on the aim** (less movement, analgesia, anxiolysis, amnesia), the child (age, compliance, development), the setting (time, staffing, load, GA availability) and the procedure (emergency vs planned, length, intensity).
claims.source_text: Choice of agent depends on the aims of sedation (eg reduce movement, analgesia, anxiolysis, amnesia) and the following factors: Child factors Age, compliance, developmental stage … Environment/location factors Time of the day, staff availability, departmental load and acuity, availability of other options (eg general anaesthesia) … Procedural factors Emergency (joint relocation) vs planned (laceration repair) Length of procedure time Complexity, intensity of the stimulus of the procedure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chloral hydrate:** oral, but **narrow therapeutic index** and no analgesia.
claims.source_text: Chloral hydrate # Oral Narrow therapeutic index No analgesic effect
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Midazolam:** oral, intranasal, buccal, IM or IV; amnestic, anxiolytic, quick and short acting — but **can cause a paradoxical effect after discharge**, may fail, and gives no analgesia.
claims.source_text: Midazolam # Oral, intranasal, buccal, IM or IV Amnestic and anxiolytic effect Quick onset Short acting Can produce paradoxical effect after discharge Agent failure No analgesic effect
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intranasal fentanyl:** synergistic with nitrous oxide and avoids IV access, but no sedative effect. **Nitrous oxide:** quick on and off, anxiolysis and amnesia; vomiting is common and analgesia limited.
claims.source_text: Intranasal fentanyl Synergistic with nitrous oxide Reduces need for IV access No sedative effect Nitrous oxide Quick onset and offset Anxiolysis and amnesia Vomiting is common Limited analgesic effect
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ketamine:** airway reflexes kept, cardiovascular stability, IM or IV, excellent analgesia and sedation — **can be a sole agent**; agitation and emesis in recovery, rarely laryngospasm.
claims.source_text: Ketamine* Airway reflexes maintained Cardiovascular stability IM or IV Provides excellent analgesia and sedation and thus can be used as a sole procedural agent Side effects include agitation and emesis during recovery Rarely can cause laryngospasm
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Propofol:** ultrashort-acting, good muscle relaxation (eg ankle dislocation) — but ⚠️ **narrow therapeutic window, respiratory and cardiovascular depression, and no analgesia.**
claims.source_text: Propofol #* Ultrashort acting sedative anaesthetic agent Effective for muscle relaxation (eg reduction of ankle dislocation) Narrow therapeutic window Respiratory and cardiovascular depression Lack of analgesic property
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chloral hydrate, midazolam and propofol may need extra analgesia** (eg fentanyl) for painful procedures. ⚠️ **Ketamine and propofol only by clinicians trained and approved in their use, with advanced airway experience.**
claims.source_text: Chloral hydrate # … Midazolam # … Propofol #* … # Extra analgesia eg fentanyl may be required for painful procedures when using these drugs * Ketamine and propofol should only be used by clinicians who are trained and approved in their use and who have experience in paediatric resuscitation, advanced airway management and monitoring
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Monitor pulse oximetry, cardiac rhythm and blood pressure, watch airway and chest movement closely, and keep skilled staff present until recovery is well established.**
claims.source_text: Pulse oximetry, cardiac monitoring and blood pressure Close observation of the airway and chest movements is necessary Appropriately skilled staff in attendance until recovery is well established
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not discharge until back to premorbid neurological baseline** — walking and talking at the pre-treatment level.
claims.source_text: The child should not be discharged home until they have returned to their premorbid neurological baseline … Child is able to ambulate and verbalise at a level consistent with their pre-treatment neurological baseline
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If sedation fails:** try an alternative if safe; involve the paediatric team if a general anaesthetic is needed; **transfer if needs exceed local capability.**
claims.source_text: Trial of alternative sedation choice, if safe and appropriate to do so … Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Sedation failure and general anaesthetic required … Consider transfer when Sedation and analgesia requirements exceed local capabilities
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Procedural sedation' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Procedural_sedation/, retrieved 2026-09-23
